qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Specialty materials qualified into customer engineering, safety, and regulatory specifications create customer switching barriers (Tyvek, Kevlar, Nomex, FilmTec water filtration). However, fails proof of moat with a 10-year median ROIC of ~7.8% and 2024–2026 ROIC hovering at 3.4%–4.1%, well below the 12% hurdle and failing to exceed cost of capital. Key erosion threats include cyclical end-market swings, customer substitution, raw material inflation, and lingering legacy environmental (PFAS) liabilities.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC < 12%, REJECT). DuPont fails the Munger proof-of-moat requirement with a 10-year median ROIC of ~7.8% and 2024–2026 ROIC languishing at 3.4%–4.1%, consistently trailing its ~8% cost of capital. Despite switching costs in qualified specialty materials (Tyvek, Kevlar, Nomex, water filtration membranes), serial corporate restructurings (DowDuPont separation, Celanese divestiture, Qnity Electronics spinoff), recurring asset write-downs, cyclical end-market exposure, and substantial legacy PFAS liabilities prevent economic value creation.
qualitative.evidence: Empirical capital efficiency over the trailing decade shows structural inability to clear the 12% ROIC hurdle: 10-year median ROIC is 7.8% and average ROIC is below 4% due to large asset impairments, restructuring charges, and cyclical troughs. In 2024–2026, ROIC remained depressed at 3.4%–4.1% against an ~8% WACC. Free cash flow generation has been volatile ($473M in FY2024, $227M standard / $689M transaction-adjusted in FY2025, ~$793M TTM in 2026), heavily burdened by separation transaction expenses and ongoing multi-billion-dollar PFAS legacy liabilities. The core business lacks the pricing power and reinvestment returns required of an elite compounder.
